title: Sandbox stdout/stderr output cap
description: Sandboxed runs return whatever the program wrote, so a runaway `print` loop ships megabytes of stdout through `CodeExecutionOutput` into the response file. Add a configurable byte budget for the stdout/stderr that `SandboxCodeExecutionBackend` returns, with the capping rule itself in a new pure module `src/bespokelabs/curator/code_executor/output_cap.py` (a pure function of its arguments — no clock, randomness or I/O) exporting: `DEFAULT_MAX_OUTPUT_BYTES: int = 65536`; a real `@dataclass(frozen=True)` (not a pydantic model, `NamedTuple`, dict or tuple) `CappedStream` with fields, in this declaration order, `text: str | None`, `truncated: bool`, `original_bytes: int`, `kept_bytes: int`; a frozen `StreamCapReport` with fields, in this order, `stdout: str | None`, `stderr: str | None`, `truncated_streams: list[str]`; and two functions `cap_stream(data: str | bytes | None, max_bytes: int = DEFAULT_MAX_OUTPUT_BYTES) -> CappedStream` and `cap_execution_streams(stdout: str | bytes | None, stderr: str | bytes | None, max_bytes: int = DEFAULT_MAX_OUTPUT_BYTES) -> StreamCapReport`. `original_bytes` is the UTF-8 byte length of the input (`0` for `None`), `kept_bytes` is the byte count of the input's surviving portion, `truncated` says whether the stream was shortened, and `text` is `None` only when `data is None` (a null stream is never coerced to `""`). In `types.py`, `CodeExecutionBackendConfig` gains `max_output_bytes: int = Field(default=65536, ge=0)` — `_factory.py:31` already does `CodeExecutionBackendConfig(**backend_params)`, so it is reachable as `CodeExecutor(backend_params={"max_output_bytes": ...})` for every backend name with no factory edit, and a negative value must be rejected at construction with pydantic's `ValidationError`; `CodeExecutionResult` and `CodeExecutionOutput` each gain a non-Optional `truncated_streams: list[str] = []` naming which of `"stdout"`/`"stderr"` were shortened on that run (a stream that is `None`, empty or under budget contributes nothing), and the field must survive `CodeExecutionResponse(...).model_dump()`. In `code_execution_backend/sandbox_backend.py`, `__init__` sets `self.max_output_bytes: int`, `execute_request` passes `max_output_bytes=self.max_output_bytes` into the existing `partial(_execute_in_sandbox, ...)`, and the module-level function becomes `_execute_in_sandbox(code, code_input, timeout, backend_name, sandbox_kwargs, *, max_output_bytes: int = DEFAULT_MAX_OUTPUT_BYTES)` — keyword-only after a bare `*`, so a positional sixth argument raises `TypeError`. Capping applies at all four `CodeExecutionOutput` construction sites: success, the `exit_code == 124` timeout, the non-zero exit, and the `except Exception` path whose streams come from `getattr(result, "stdout", None)` and may be `None`. The existing error-message and file-collection helpers keep their current signatures and message text, and `files` is not capped; nothing in `_factory.py`, `code_executor.py` or `db.py` changes. Python 3.10, pydantic >=2.9.2, no new dependency; the whole thing must be testable directly and through the fake `bespokelabs.sandbox` module seam already used by `tests/code_executor/test_sandbox_backend.py`.

requirement.rule:
When a stream exceeds the budget the kept payload is the FIRST `(max_bytes * 3) // 4` UTF-8 bytes followed by the LAST `max_bytes - (max_bytes * 3) // 4` bytes (floor division; for `max_bytes=64` that is 48 head + 16 tail), with the middle dropped. The two pieces are joined by exactly `ELISION_MARKER_TEMPLATE: str = "
[[curator:elided {dropped} bytes]]
"` (also exported from `output_cap`), where `{dropped}` is the decimal count of bytes actually thrown away, i.e. `original_bytes - kept_bytes`, never `original_bytes - max_bytes`, and with no thousands separator. The marker is OUTSIDE the budget: `kept_bytes` never counts it, and the returned `text` is longer than `max_bytes` by exactly the marker's length. Observable: `cap_stream("0123456789" * 10, 64)` == `CappedStream(text="012345678901234567890123456789012345678901234567" + "
[[curator:elided 36 bytes]]
" + "4567890123456789", truncated=True, original_bytes=100, kept_bytes=64)`, so `len(text) == 93` (48 + 29 + 16) and the marker starts at offset 48.
requirement.scope: The budget is counted in UTF-8 bytes and both slices are trimmed to codepoint boundaries before decoding: for the head try cutting 0, 1, 2 then 3 trailing bytes and take the first candidate that `bytes.decode("utf-8")` accepts; for the tail try dropping 0, 1, 2 then 3 LEADING bytes and take the first that decodes. Only if no candidate within three bytes decodes (genuinely invalid UTF-8, not merely split) is the untrimmed slice decoded with `errors="replace"`. Consequently `kept_bytes` may be strictly LESS than `max_bytes`, and clean multi-byte input never yields U+FFFD. Observable: `cap_stream("€" * 10, 20)` == `CappedStream("€€€€€\n[[curator:elided 12 bytes]]\n€", True, 30, 18)` — `kept_bytes == 18` not 20, `"�" not in text`, exactly six `€` in the text.
requirement.exclusions_or_crossover: `max_bytes == 0` is the sentinel for *unlimited* and must NOT be treated as "keep nothing" nor as a sub-floor value: `cap_stream("A" * 100000, 0)` returns `CappedStream("A" * 100000, False, 100000, 100000)` — the whole stream, `truncated=False`, `kept_bytes == original_bytes`, no marker and no exception, even though `0 < 16`. Every other value below the floor is rejected. `CodeExecutionBackendConfig(max_output_bytes=0)` therefore constructs and means "no capping", while the `Field(..., ge=0)` rejection of negatives is unchanged.
requirement.failure_behavior: `output_cap` exports `MIN_MAX_OUTPUT_BYTES: int = 16` and `class OutputCapError(ValueError)` whose `__init__(self, max_bytes: int)` stores `self.max_bytes` and formats the message `f"max_bytes must be 0 or at least {MIN_MAX_OUTPUT_BYTES}, got {max_bytes}"`. `cap_stream` — and therefore `cap_execution_streams` — raises it whenever `max_bytes != 0 and max_bytes < 16`, i.e. for negatives and for 1..15. The check runs BEFORE the `data is None` check, so `cap_stream(None, 8)` raises rather than returning. Observables: `pytest.raises(OutputCapError)` for `cap_stream(b"x", 15)`, `cap_stream(b"x", 1)`, `cap_stream(b"x", -1)`, `cap_stream(None, 8)`, each with `exc.value.max_bytes` equal to the offending value and `isinstance(exc.value, ValueError) is True`; `cap_stream(b"x", 16)` does not raise and returns `CappedStream("x", False, 1, 1)`.
requirement.observability: `truncated_streams` is sorted ALPHABETICALLY, not in stream-read/argument/field order, so the only possible values are `[]`, `["stderr"]`, `["stdout"]` and `["stderr", "stdout"]`. Observables: `cap_execution_streams("A" * 300, "B" * 300, 64).truncated_streams == ["stderr", "stdout"]` (exactly that order); `cap_execution_streams("A" * 300, None, 64).truncated_streams == ["stdout"]`; `cap_execution_streams("a", "b", 64).truncated_streams == []`; and the same alphabetical list reaches `CodeExecutionOutput.truncated_streams` from `_execute_in_sandbox` (fake sandbox with `exit_code=1, stdout="0123456789" * 10, stderr="E" * 80`, budget 64 → `["stderr", "stdout"]`).

fragmentation_sources: chat thread arguing head-only vs tail-only vs both ends, settling on 3:1 because the traceback tail is what people actually read
wiki page fixing the marker spelling and stating that the notice is charged outside the budget
a bug report where a truncated dump came back full of replacement characters, plus the reply setting the three-byte boundary allowance
mail thread on what a zero budget should mean and why the floor is 16
hidden_requirements.earlier_reversed_version: an earlier revision reserved room for the marker inside the budget (so the returned text was never longer than max_bytes) and reported the dropped count as original_bytes - max_bytes; it was reversed because the two counts disagreed once boundary trimming shortened the payload

requirement.rule: On the `except Exception` path of `_execute_in_sandbox` the exception text is itself capped with the same budget and the same head/tail rule as a stream: `error = cap_stream(str(e), max_output_bytes).text`, so it is shortened rather than passed through. Observable, with a fake sandbox returning `exit_code=0, stdout="A" * 300, stderr=""` whose `__exit__` raises `RuntimeError("X" * 300)` at `max_output_bytes=64`: `output.error == "X" * 48 + "\n[[curator:elided 236 bytes]]\n" + "X" * 16` (`len == 94`), alongside `len(output.stdout) == 94` and `output.truncated_streams == ["stdout"]`. With `RuntimeError("boom")` instead, `output.error == "boom"` exactly. The timeout message `f"Execution timed out after {timeout}s"` is curator's own text and is never capped.
requirement.exclusions_or_crossover:
The non-zero-exit path must feed the exit-code error helper the CAPPED stderr instead of `result.stderr` (closing the leak where the full stderr rides out inside `error`), and the assembled message is then left alone — it is NOT re-capped, and its ~50-character prefix is allowed to push it past the budget. Observable, fake sandbox with `exit_code=1, stderr="E" * 80, stdout=""`, budget 64: `output.error == "Program exited with status code 1

Error details:
" + output.stderr` with `output.stderr == "E" * 48 + "
[[curator:elided 16 bytes]]
" + "E" * 16`, so `len(output.error) == 143` — not 130 (raw stderr) and not 94 (message re-capped). `files` is still never capped.
requirement.observability: `CodeExecutionOutput` gains a non-Optional `error_truncated: bool = False`, declared immediately after `truncated_streams`; `CodeExecutionResult` does NOT get it. It is `True` on exactly one path — the `except Exception` path, and only when the cap actually shortened `str(e)`; it stays `False` everywhere else, including the non-zero-exit path whose `error` embeds a stderr that *was* truncated. Observables: `"error_truncated" not in CodeExecutionResult.model_fields`; `CodeExecutionOutput().error_truncated is False` and `model_fields["error_truncated"].is_required() is False`; on the `RuntimeError("X" * 300)` fake `output.error_truncated is True` while `output.truncated_streams == ["stdout"]` (the string `"error"` never appears in that list); on the `exit_code=1, stderr="E" * 80` fake `output.error_truncated is False` with `output.truncated_streams == ["stderr"]`; and `sorted(CodeExecutionResponse(exec_output=CodeExecutionOutput(error="x", error_truncated=True)).model_dump()["exec_output"]) == ["error", "error_truncated", "files", "message", "stderr", "stdout", "truncated_streams"]`.
requirement.scope: `output_cap` exports `TRUNCATION_LOG_TEMPLATE: str = "sandbox output capped: {streams} exceeded the {budget}-byte budget"`, and `_execute_in_sandbox` emits it through the module's existing `logger` at WARNING level (the module otherwise uses `logger.debug`) exactly once per run: immediately after capping the streams inside the `with` block, and only when the truncated-stream list is non-empty — so the success, timeout and non-zero-exit returns share that one call site. `{streams}` is `", ".join(...)` of the truncated names and `{budget}` is the effective `max_output_bytes`. The `except`-path salvage cap and the error cap of this requirement do NOT log. Observables with `monkeypatch.setattr(sandbox_backend, "logger", recorder)` and budget 64: `stdout="A" * 300, stderr=""` → `recorder.warnings == ["sandbox output capped: stdout exceeded the 64-byte budget"]`; the same run whose `__exit__` raises `RuntimeError("X" * 300)` → that same single line, not two; `stdout="A", stderr="B"` → `[]`; `stdout="A" * 300` with `max_output_bytes=0` → `[]`; `exit_code=124, stdout="A" * 300` → one line; `execute_command` raising `RuntimeError("kaboom")` → `[]`.

fragmentation_sources: incident thread where a 40 MB traceback shipped inside the `error` field even after the stream fields were bounded
review comment insisting the exit-code message keep its full assembled length while the stderr it embeds is bounded
wiki note introducing the per-output flag and arguing it belongs on the output model only, since the result model has no error field
chat about log volume, fixing the warning level, the exact template wording and the one-line-per-run rule
hidden_requirements.earlier_reversed_version: the flag was first spelled `error_capped` and set `True` on the non-zero-exit path too (any error text affected by capping); it was reversed so it reports only text the cap actually clipped, leaving the assembled exit-code message at False
